stem: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
body: Dear Ms. Rivera, Our community garden club will hold its first seed exchange next Saturday at the old library hall. Since you have grown rare tomatoes for years, we would be honored if you could share a few seeds and a short story about how you keep them healthy. Please let me know by Wednesday whether you can join us. Warm regards, Daniel Ortiz

stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
body: When students explain an idea to a classmate, they often discover gaps they did not notice while reading alone. Speaking forces them to put steps in order and to choose words that someone else can follow. For this reason, a short pair explanation after reading can do more for understanding than a second silent reading.

stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
body: Maps are useful precisely because they leave things out. A city map that showed every tree, crack, and parked car would be as large and as confusing as the city itself. What makes a map helpful is its willingness to _____, keeping only what a traveler needs for a particular purpose.

stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
body: A runner who checks a watch every few seconds may actually run slower. Constant measuring pulls attention away from breathing and stride, the very things that create speed. In many skills, performance improves when we _____ for a while and let practiced movements work on their own.

stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
body: Bread dough that sits overnight in a cool room tastes different from dough baked right away. (A) As the yeast works slowly, it produces small amounts of acids and other flavors. (B) The cold slows the yeast, giving it more time to break down starches. (C) These compounds build up hour by hour, which is why patient bakers often get richer bread.

stem: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.
body: Some birds hide thousands of seeds each autumn. ( ① ) Remarkably, they find most of them months later under snow. ( ② ) Scientists once thought the birds simply searched everywhere. ( ③ ) Careful tests showed otherwise. ( ④ ) The birds remember landmarks such as rocks and trees around each hiding place. ( ⑤ ) When researchers moved the landmarks, the birds dug in the wrong spots.
